rationale: Eleventh investigation, taking up the verification path that the overview recorded as unread: the quorum accounting of the leader's own leadership check. Reading the path showed that the numerator and the denominator of that check come from different sets. verifyLeader sets the future's votes to one for the leader and quorumSize to r.quorumSize(), which counts only voters, but it registers the future with every follower replication state, non-voters included, and each replication goroutine adds one vote as soon as its heartbeat RPC succeeds. A leader of a two-voter configuration therefore reaches the required two votes with its own vote plus the acknowledgement of a single non-voter, although the voter majority it claims to have confirmed is not reachable. The harness fixes exactly that case and is deterministic, and the map already carries the needed basis: the fact f-leadership-held, its consumer b-client-apply-verify, the heartbeat behaviour b-heartbeat-liveness and the lease behaviour b-leader-lease-stepdown, with the existing material s-api-verify-leader for the accessor.

candidate.rationale: New Candidate opened from the unread verification path. It states that a leadership confirmation may rest only on acknowledgements from voters, and binds it to VerifyLeader, which registers verification with every replication state while sizing the quorum by voters alone.

question.question: May Raft.VerifyLeader report success when the leader of the captured module has heard only from itself and from a server that is not a voter, although the quorum it claims to have confirmed is the majority of the voting configuration, or must the confirmation rest on voter acknowledgements only?
question.importance: VerifyLeader exists so that a caller does not return stale data from the FSM after the peer has lost leadership, which makes its answer the guard for the read-index and lease-read patterns the accessor is documented for. If the confirmation can be satisfied by a non-voter's heartbeat while the voter majority is unreachable, a leader that has in fact lost the ability to reach its voters still tells its callers that it is the leader, and a client that trusts the answer can serve a read that the rest of the cluster has already superseded. The acknowledgement counted this way is an ordinary successful heartbeat, so the path is on the shipped transport and needs no failure injection beyond removing a route.
participants: the voter the leader can no longer reach
the non-voter that still answers heartbeats
objects: the follower replication state map and its notify sets
the successful heartbeat response of the non-voter
contexts: a three-server configuration with two voters and one non-voter
the prefix after the leader's route to the other voter is removed and before any lease expiry or election
event_paths: verification path: VerifyLeader hands the future to the main loop, verifyLeader sets the leader's own vote, sizes the quorum from the voters, registers the future in every replication state and triggers immediate heartbeats
acknowledgement path: the non-voter's replication goroutine completes its heartbeat and votes for the future, which reaches the quorum number
result path: the future is answered and the caller reads its error

supporting_behavior_ids.b-heartbeat-liveness: the per-peer heartbeat goroutine that delivers the acknowledgements which are counted as votes, and the reason a non-voter's answer can reach the future at all
supporting_behavior_ids.b-leader-lease-stepdown: the lease check that counts only voters for the same question, which shows the voter-only basis the verification path does not apply

counterevidence: The leader is still in the leader state when the verification answers, so the answer is not wrong about the node's own view; the claim is about the quorum the accessor is documented to confirm.
No source states that the heartbeat acknowledgement of a non-voter was intended to count toward verification.
A caller that ignores VerifyLeader and reads the FSM directly is unaffected.
The map's overview recorded this path as not traced to completion, so a part of the accounting not exercised here may still be unread.
unknowns: whether the counted acknowledgements were intended to be filtered by suffrage
whether the repair filters the votes or stops registering non-voter replication states for verification
which consumers outside the module rely on the confirmation, which would raise the consequence
question.trigger_rationale: verifyLeader counts the leader's own vote, sizes the quorum with quorumSize(), which iterates only servers whose suffrage is Voter, and then registers the future with every entry of the follower replication state map, which is built from all servers of the configuration, non-voters included. Each replication goroutine votes for the future when its heartbeat succeeds, so the count can include a non-voter while the threshold counts voters only. The harness makes the two sets visibly different by using a two-voter configuration with one non-voter and removing the leader's route to the other voter: the reachable acknowledgements are the leader itself and the non-voter, which is exactly the quorum number.

obligation.description: Raft.VerifyLeader may report success only when a quorum of the voting configuration of the leader's term has acknowledged within that verification: acknowledgements from servers that are not voters may not be counted toward that quorum, because the future is documented as the guard against returning stale data after leadership is lost.

scope.description: A leader in the captured module whose latest configuration contains non-voters and whose only reachable peer is a non-voter, observed before any lease expiry or election changes its state.
assumptions: the caller reads the future's error as the answer to whether the node is still the leader
the configuration used by quorumSize and the configuration whose replication states receive the future are the same latest configuration
excluded: the correctness of the leader state itself, which the check reads back
the lease-based step-down path, which is a separate mechanism
any requirement on callers or transports outside the module

pending: whether the intended repair filters votes by suffrage or excludes non-voter replication states from verification
which consumers rely on the confirmation

grounding.derivation: VerifyLeader is documented as the guard against returning stale data after the peer has lost leadership and hands a verifyFuture to the main loop (s-api-verify-leader). There verifyLeader counts the leader's own vote, sizes the quorum with r.quorumSize(), which counts only servers whose suffrage is Voter (s-raft-candidate-vote, s-raft-leader-lease), and registers the future with every follower replication state, which the leader populates from all servers of the latest configuration, non-voters included. Each replication goroutine adds one vote when its heartbeat RPC succeeds (s-replication-heartbeat). The confirmation can therefore be satisfied by a non-voter while the voter majority is unreachable, which contradicts the quorum the accessor claims to confirm, so the obligation requires voter acknowledgements only.
grounding.applicability: Applies to any leader whose configuration contains non-voters. The check exercises a two-voter configuration with one non-voter and removes the leader's route to the other voter, with timeouts long enough that the leader has not stepped down when the verification is issued.
unresolved: whether counting a non-voter's acknowledgement is deliberate, which no source states
which consumers depend on the confirmation
alternatives: the success could be read as 'the leader still believes it is the leader', but the accessor's contract is a quorum confirmation, and the belief itself is what the caller is trying to test

associations.rationale: This entry point is the located implementation of the confirmation duty: it returns the future whose error is the leadership answer, while the quorum it must satisfy is computed from the voters and the acknowledgements it accepts come from every member of the configuration.

bindings.description: Raft.VerifyLeader hands a verifyFuture to the leader's main loop and returns it to the caller as the answer to whether the node is still the leader; the loop sizes the quorum from the voters but registers the future with every follower replication state, non-voters included, so a non-voter's heartbeat acknowledgement can complete the confirmation.
pending: whether the votes should be filtered by suffrage or non-voter replication states excluded from verification
